expected_output.reasoning:
The response does a solid job on most substantive criteria: it enumerates guardrails across the account, resolves which guardrail (if any) is referenced by the customer-facing runtime, identifies the exposure (no guardrail wired into the support assistant's env vars or IAM role), distinguishes enforced vs DRAFT guardrails (calling out that some DRAFT guardrails serve traffic and that the strongest guardrail is only DRAFT), prescribes read-only remediation steps (publish a numbered version, attach it, add IAM condition), and discloses uncovered paths/checks (code in S3 it couldn't read, Lambda it couldn't inspect, possible paths outside the account).

However, it fails two explicit, checkable requirements:
1. It never cites an LLM-GRD check-id (e.g., LLM-GRD-001) with severity and an AWS-doc citation for findings, as the expected output explicitly requires ("raises LLM-GRD-001 at CRITICAL ... cites an LLM-GRD check-id with its severity and an AWS-doc citation for each finding"). The response has no check-id taxonomy, no severity labels, and no AWS documentation citations anywhere.
2. It explicitly prints the raw 12-digit account ID: "I checked account 012345678901_1, the only associated account, in us-east-1, us-west-2 and us-east-2." This directly violates "It never prints a raw 12-digit account ID."

These are concrete, unambiguous violations of the expected output criteria, so the response fails despite being otherwise thorough and well-reasoned.
expected_output.evidence: "I checked account 012345678901_1, the only associated account, in us-east-1, us-west-2 and us-east-2." — raw account ID printed. Also, no LLM-GRD-### check-id, severity label, or AWS documentation citation appears anywhere in the response.

assertion_results.evidence: The agent explicitly checked whether the production runtime has a guardrail wired in: "No guardrail is wired in. The runtime's only environment variables are CALL_MODEL, MODEL_ID and SERVICE_NAME. None of them carries a guardrail ID or version." It also checked IAM role permissions and account-wide policies before concluding exposure, rather than assuming a guardrail was attached.
assertion_results.reasoning: The agent actively investigated the production path (the AgentCore runtime) for guardrail references (env vars, IAM permissions, account-level enforcement) before concluding no guardrail exists, which satisfies the assertion's requirement to resolve which guardrail/version is referenced rather than assume protection exists.

assertion_results.text: The response reports the concrete observed value that triggered each finding (for example no guardrailIdentifier on the invocation, or content filters at NONE) rather than a generic statement
assertion_results.evidence: Concrete values cited include: "The runtime's only environment variables are CALL_MODEL, MODEL_ID and SERVICE_NAME", "Its model ID is us.amazon.nova-micro-v9:0", "Content filters: hate and insults only", "Denied topics: 'Legal advice' only", "PII: email addresses only, which are anonymized", "pinned to version 1", guardrail IDs like 31dftpj9p7bd and 3h154od4rp5h, and "About 10,000 claude-sonnet-5 calls in 14 days had no guardrail metrics."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response consistently backs findings with specific observed values (env var names, model IDs, guardrail IDs, filter categories, counts of logged events) rather than vague generic statements, satisfying the assertion.

assertion_results.text: The response prescribes only read-only remediations the user runs themselves and does not claim to have modified any resource
assertion_results.evidence: The agent states 'Everything I did was read-only.' and in the 'What I'd do' section phrases all remediation steps as actions for the user: 'Someone with S3 read access needs to do this', 'Publish a numbered version of a strong guardrail... Add a grounding check, attach it to the support assistant, and grant the role the needed permissions', 'Add a bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier condition...', 'Set a retention period on the invocation log group.'
assertion_results.reasoning: No claim of having modified any resource appears; all remediation items are prescribed as actions the user or team should take, and the agent explicitly confirms its own activity was read-only.

assertion_results.text: The response discloses which paths, regions, or checks it could not cover rather than implying full coverage
assertion_results.evidence: The agent discloses coverage limits explicitly: "I checked account 012345678901_1, the only associated account, in us-east-1, us-west-2 and us-east-2. Only us-east-1 has Bedrock resources." Also: "The main caveat: I couldn't read the runtime's code, because S3 and Lambda reads are denied to my role." and "I also couldn't see any organization-level policy, though I can't rule one out." and "I can't tell whether the real customer-facing path runs somewhere outside this account."
assertion_results.reasoning: The response explicitly lists multiple scope limitations (regions checked, inability to read code, inability to see org-level policy, uncertainty about paths outside the account), satisfying the assertion that it discloses what it could not cover rather than implying full coverage.
